subject: Clarify order form: auto-renew timing & termination-for-convenience carveouts
body:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify order form: auto-renew timing & termination-for-convenience carveouts

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We reviewed Acme's redlines and wanted to pull a couple items into a short thread so we can align quickly on the Order Form language before legal does a formal pass. Two things came up that we think are material to the commercial terms and operational handoff: auto-renew notice window and the termination-for-convenience (TFC) mechanics.

Quick problem statement: Acme's proposed 90-day opt-out for auto-renew and a TFC obligation that would require payment for the remainder of the Term creates forecasting and capacity constraints on our side (we reserve Dedicated pools). We want to propose a compromise that preserves Acme's ability to plan while keeping Redwood's capacity and billing model predictable.

Ask: can Acme accept the compromise language below, and will you loop in outside counsel if you want to change legal wording? If this is acceptable, I can have our legal (Laura) produce a redline.

Proposed compromise (high level) — what Redwood would be comfortable with:
- Auto-renew opt-out: Customer must give written notice at least 60 days prior to the renewal effective date (instead of Acme's requested 90 days).
- Termination for convenience: Customer may terminate after a 90-day notice; Customer pays for services through the effective termination date and any non-cancellable committed capacity fees for a 90-day wind‑down (we would pro-rate consumed usage). Redwood to provide reasonable cutover/transfer support for 30 days after termination at standard rates.

Why this helps both parties: it shortens our capacity planning tail while giving Acme a three-month runway to migrate or scale down. It also keeps the termination payment exposure contained while giving Acme predictability on transition support.

Attachments: I attached the latest Order Form with Acme's inline notes (Acme_OrderForm_redlines.docx) and a copy of our MSA for reference (Redwood_MSA_v3_redline.pdf).

If that compromise looks reasonable, please say so and we will circulate a legal redline by EOD Thursday.

Best,
Rishi
--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify order form: auto-renew timing & termination-for-convenience carveouts

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the concise framing.

A few immediate points from Acme's side:
- We proposed 90 days because our procurement cycle is aligned to quarter planning and a 60-day notice would make it difficult for us to line up replacement capacity / budget.
- On TFC, Acme's expectation is that the vendor (Redwood) should absorb more of the risk if we terminate for convenience — specifically, we asked for payment of only the then‑current monthly recurring fees through the termination effective date, not additional committed capacity fees.

I've attached our version with inline comments (Acme_OrderForm_redlines.docx). Please see page 3 for the specific TFC draft. I'm looping in Andrew (outside counsel) to help with legal framing; he'll likely suggest alternate language that preserves our rights.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept Acme's ask of no post-termination committed capacity payment? If not, what exact alternative language would Redwood propose so procurement can rapidly review?

Cheers,
Sarah

Hi Laura / Karthik —

Looping you both in. Acme pushed back on our 60-day opt-out and on the committed capacity payment for TFC — they want no post-termination committed fees. They cite procurement rhythm and risk allocation to vendors.

Karthik — can you confirm whether the Dedicated pool commitment in this deal is sized with any hard non-cancellable months beyond the order term? I want to understand operational exposure if we agree to Acme's ask.

Laura — if Acme insist on no post-termination capacity payments, what is Redwood's lowest-risk legal compromise to offer (preserve forecasting, limit financial exposure)? If you can draft a couple of short language options we can include in the vendor redline, that will speed negotiation.

Thanks — I want to keep this concise so we can present a single counter to Acme tomorrow.

Rishi


-----Original Message-----
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>; Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme.com>; Andrew Cho <andrew@lawfirmllp.com>

Subject: RE: Clarify order form: auto-renew timing & termination-for-convenience carveouts

Rishi / team / Sarah / Andrew —

Thanks for the context. Attached is a proposed legal redline that balances Acme's procurement needs with Redwood's operational constraints (Redwood_MSA_tfc_proposal_redline.pdf). Below is the preferred legal language and rationale.

Suggested language (clean copy for insertion into the Order Form / MSA):
"Auto-Renewal; Notice of Non‑Renewal. Unless Customer provides prior written notice of non‑renewal at least sixty (60) days before the then-current term expires, the applicable Order Form shall automatically renew for an additional term of the same duration (an "Auto‑Renewal")."

"Termination for Convenience. Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience upon at least ninety (90) days' prior written notice to Redwood. If Customer exercises this right, Customer shall pay all fees accrued and payable through the effective date of termination. Additionally, where Customer has purchased committed capacity or Reserved Capacity that was specifically allocated to Customer and reasonably non‑cancellable by Redwood for the remainder of the then-current term, Customer shall be responsible for a pro‑rated portion of such committed capacity fees covering a ninety (90) day wind‑down period from the effective date of termination; provided, however, that Redwood shall use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate such fees by offering reallocation of unused capacity to other customers or by offering credits where allocation can be avoided"

Key points / rationale:
- We kept Auto‑Renew at 60 days (compromise). 90 days is tight for Redwood's capacity model and increases our forecasting tail.
- For TFC, we accepted a Customer-friendly effective date (90 days) but limited post-termination exposure to a pro‑rated 90‑day wind‑down tied specifically to capacity that was truly non‑cancellable on our side. That reduces our gross liability while giving Acme a predictable payment window and transition runway.
- We added an obligation for Redwood to use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate committed capacity charges (reallocation or credits). This helps procurement and gives Acme comfort that we're not simply billing for unused, avoidable capacity.

Operational notes for Karthik: if Acme agrees to this approach, please send me a short note describing which portions of the dedicated pool are non-cancellable and the earliest reallocation date; we will need that for contract exhibits.

Next steps:
1) Rishi to confirm with Acme whether the 60/90 compromise is acceptable.
2) If Acme accepts in principle, Laura will send a tracked redline to both counsel for final signoff.
3) Karthik to produce a capacity attachment/exhibit that lists non‑cancellable allocations (if any).

Sarah / Andrew — happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk through language if that helps procurement sign off quickly.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
